overview: The Medford Historical Commission reviewed demolition applications, finding three properties historically significant and advancing them to preferably preserved hearings. The commission also received updates on cemetery preservation projects, recent archaeological findings at the former Cross Street Cemetery site, and ongoing survey work.

items.title: 140 Summer Street
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application and voted to find 140 Summer Street historically significant, advancing it to a preferably preserved hearing.

items.title: 31 Wilson Street
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application and determined 31 Wilson Street to be historically significant.

items.title: 4 Grove Street
items.summary: Following unauthorized porch removal, the commission accepted a demolition application and determined 4 Grove Street historically significant.

items.title: Applications for 26 Rockwell Avenue, 76 Court Street, and 115 Emerald Street
items.summary: The commission voted to accept demolition applications for 26 Rockwell Avenue, 76 Court Street, and 115 Emerald Street ahead of future significance determinations.

items.title: Oak Grove Cemetery Headstone Assessment
items.summary: Ryan Hayward presented a consultant assessment estimating roughly $70,000 to $100,000 to repair approximately 100 relocated Cross Street Cemetery gravestones at Oak Grove Cemetery.

items.title: Cross Street Cemetery Site Archaeological Findings
items.summary: Hayward reported that exploratory trenching at the former Cross Street Cemetery parcel uncovered artifacts and human remains, initiating multi-year state coordination and site investigations.

items.title: Preservation Ordinance and 27 Allmont Street
items.summary: The commission tabled preservation ordinance revisions and discussed photographic documentation and Historic District Commission outreach for 27 Allmont Street during its demolition delay.

items.title: CPA Archaeology and Neighborhood Surveys
items.summary: Hayward reported that SWCA was selected for Phase 2 archaeology at Thomas Brooks Park and outlined progress on neighborhood survey efforts in Sagamore Vale and Hastings Heights.

items.title: City Zoning and Tufts University Development
items.summary: Commissioners discussed requesting earlier coordination and notice from the Planning Department regarding citywide zoning updates and large development proposals, including a proposed Tufts dormitory.

items.title: Brooks Estate and Cemetery Parcel Updates
items.summary: Commissioners reviewed funding timelines, newsletter efforts, and access parking plans at the Brooks Estate, noting potential coordination with an adjacent cemetery parcel design.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the December 2024 meeting minutes as amended.
